clue.text: Dense nature of formal agreement leads to new extremely simple style

parts.note: a compact is a formal agreement or treaty between parties

indicators.note: the leads of words are their opening letters, taken here from the four words that follow

explanation.surface: A critic describes how a formal agreement ushered in a stark, minimalist style.
explanation.definitionFit: Being compact means closely packed, so the quality of being dense is a synonym.

clue.text: Pear with no end is highly amusing

indicators.note: the pear's name loses its final letter, as if cut short at the end

parts.note: the Comice is a well-known variety of dessert pear

explanation.surface: Someone finds a pear without its bottom hilarious.
explanation.definitionFit: Something comic makes people laugh, so it is a synonym for very funny.

clue.text: Chap makes holes in soil, we hear, finding jawbones

parts.note: a chap is a man

indicators.note: says the letters that follow sound like the gardening word, not spelt the same

parts.note: to dibble is to make holes in the ground with a dibber for planting seeds

explanation.surface: A gardener poking holes in the earth turns up some old jawbones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' means the second part only sounds like DIBBLES; the answer spells it DIBLES.
explanation.definitionFit: Mandibles are the lower jaw bones in vertebrates, or the jaw parts of insects.

clue.text: Rouse a weak, disturbed Pole

indicators.note: disturbed suggests the letters of the two words are thrown out of order

parts.note: N is the north pole, as in the abbreviation on a compass

explanation.surface: Someone wakes a feeble, troubled Polish man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disturbed' rearranges A WEAK into AWAKE; Pole is a magnetic pole, not a Polish person.
explanation.definitionFit: To rouse someone is to wake them, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Pull of urban area that's never ending

indicators.note: the word for the urban area is cut short so its final letter never comes

parts.note: a town is an urban area

explanation.surface: The attraction of a city that goes on forever.
explanation.definitionFit: To tow is to pull a vehicle behind another, and as a noun a tow is a pull.

clue.text: German prince is English reader

parts.note: a lector is a reader, in church or at a university

explanation.surface: A German nobleman turns out to be a reader of English.
explanation.walkthrough: The Electors were princes of the Holy Roman Empire entitled to vote for the Emperor.
explanation.definitionFit: An Elector was a German prince with a vote in choosing the Holy Roman Emperor.

clue.text: Craftsmen making runners-up medals?

parts.note: runners-up in a competition get the second-place medal, made of a precious grey metal, so its makers are workers in that metal

explanation.surface: A question about who makes the medals given to second place.
explanation.definitionFit: Craftsmen who work in the precious metal used for second-place awards are smiths of that metal.

clue.text: Crisis antics are anyhow in vain

indicators.note: anyhow means in a careless, haphazard way, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Clowning around in an emergency is pointless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in vain' looks like 'pointless', but here vain means conceited.
explanation.definitionFit: Vain in the sense of excessively self-admiring is a synonym for self-obsessed in this way.

clue.text: Pungent gas shells etc in back area

parts.note: ammo, short for ammunition, covers shells, bullets and the like

indicators.note: back tells the solver to read the little word in backwards

explanation.surface: A sharp-smelling gas is released by shells in some rear zone.
explanation.definitionFit: Ammonia is a colourless gas with a sharp, choking smell.

clue.text: Turn with part of the foot

parts.note: the heel is the back part of the foot

explanation.surface: A dance instruction to pivot on the back of the foot.
explanation.definitionFit: To wheel is to turn round, as soldiers or birds do.

clue.text: Food colouring company feature retails regularly

parts.note: the chin is a facial feature

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of the word that comes before it

explanation.surface: A firm's food dye regularly appears in shops.
explanation.definitionFit: Cochineal is a red dye made from crushed insects, used to colour food.

clue.text: Yearn to get unusual shorn cattle

parts.note: to long for something is to yearn for it

indicators.note: unusual signals the letters of the following word in an odd new order

explanation.surface: A farmer longs for strangely sheared cattle.
explanation.definitionFit: Longhorns are a breed of cattle with long horns, such as the Texas Longhorn.

clue.text: Draw connection

definitions.meaning: a match that ends level is a draw
a link or bond between people or things

explanation.definitionFit: A game ending level is a tie, and a bond such as a family tie is a connection.

clue.text: More than one stole from playwright — like Shakespeare at first

parts.note: George Bernard Shaw was an Irish playwright

indicators.note: takes the opening letter of each of the two words before it

explanation.surface: A dramatist stole from another, in the manner of Shakespeare initially.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stole' looks like a verb (stealing from a playwright) but is a noun: a scarf.
explanation.definitionFit: A stole is a long scarf worn over the shoulders, so several are wraps of this kind.

clue.text: One helping criminal sounding like a chancer

indicators.note: the phrase that follows is said aloud and gives the answer's sound, not its spelling

parts.note: a chancer who takes a gamble is a better, one who bets

explanation.surface: An accomplice resembles an opportunist.
explanation.definitionFit: An abettor encourages or assists someone in committing a crime.

clue.text: Artist painting restorer reveals

indicators.note: the two words before reveal a name sitting within their letters

explanation.surface: A restorer at work on a painting uncovers the original artist.
explanation.walkthrough: Jean-Auguste-Dominique Ingres was a French Neoclassical painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Ingres was a nineteenth-century French painter, so an example of a painter.

clue.text: Bird to spoil metal container

parts.note: to mar something is to spoil it
a tin is a metal can or container

explanation.surface: A bird damages a metal can.
explanation.definitionFit: The house martin and sand martin are small birds of the swallow family.

clue.text: Perhaps hail one Conservative European

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: A Conservative European is perhaps hailed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hail' looks like a greeting, but it is frozen precipitation, and 'Perhaps' says it is one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Hail is pellets of frozen rain, an example of frozen water.

clue.text: Cooked patties to eat good, hot pasta

indicators.note: eating takes something inside, so one set of letters swallows the other
cooked suggests the word is worked over into a new form

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: Patties are cooked to go with some good, hot pasta.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cooked' rearranges PATTIES into SPAETTI, which takes in G and H.
explanation.definitionFit: Spaghetti is long thin strands of pasta, an example of the food.

clue.text: Has confidence in removing last ton for supporting framework

indicators.note: the final occurrence of the named letter is taken away

parts.note: someone who has confidence in a person trusts them

explanation.surface: Someone relies on taking away the last of the weight to support a structure.
explanation.definitionFit: A truss is a framework of beams supporting a roof or bridge.

clue.text: Venerated symbol to note, followed by millions

parts.note: te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale
M is the abbreviation for million

explanation.surface: A sacred emblem is worth noting, and millions follow it.
explanation.definitionFit: A totem is an object or animal revered as an emblem by a clan or group.

clue.text: Low satellite terminated prematurely

indicators.note: the word is ended early, losing its last letter

parts.note: the moon is the Earth's natural satellite

explanation.surface: A satellite in a low orbit is brought down early.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Low' looks like an adjective about orbit, but it is the verb for a cow's call.
explanation.definitionFit: To low is to make the sound a cow makes, a verb shared with the cow's call.

clue.text: Cast, we hear, is finished

indicators.note: says the word for cast is said aloud, giving a different spelling

parts.note: to cast is to throw, and the past tense is threw

explanation.surface: An actor learns the cast is done.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast' looks like actors in a play, but it is the past tense of throw.
explanation.definitionFit: Being through with something means having finished it.

clue.text: People like Disney sort actions that must move

indicators.note: the letters must move around into a fresh order

explanation.surface: Animators at a studio sort out the action sequences.
explanation.definitionFit: Walt Disney drew animated films, so he and his like are animators of drawn films.
